blocks.subtitle: Your cellular training
blocks.claim: Eight sport-relevant microRNAs from a single drop of capillary blood, translated into seven assessments covering nutrition, recovery and performance — complemented by four genetic variants.
blocks.benefit: Nutrition, recovery, training load: where your client can start.

blocks.caption: The principle
blocks.title: How to read this report.
blocks.lead: Regular training changes the body right down to the cellular level. These processes leave traces in the form of circulating microRNAs — small RNA molecules that regulate how strongly particular genes are actually expressed. Unlike genetics, these values can change, which makes them the trend component of the analysis.

cards.title: Nutritional status
cards.text: Vitamin and micronutrient requirements as well as fluid balance. Assessments: nutritional status, hydration status.

cards.title: Recovery
cards.text: Capacity to recover, training load and inflammatory activity. Assessments: injury risk, load level, inflammation.

cards.title: Performance
cards.text: Endurance capacity and the condition of the musculature. Assessments: cardiovascular fitness, muscle status.

flow.title: Measure
flow.text: Dried blood spot card, fingertip. Eight microRNAs and four genetic variants. No fasting required.

flow.title: Assess
flow.text: The microRNAs feed into seven assessments on the traffic light 1–9. Each assessment combines several markers.

flow.title: Adjust
flow.text: Targeted recommendations on training, recovery and phytonutrients — plus follow-up monitoring.

blocks.scaleTitle: How do I read the scale?
blocks.scaleLead: All assessments and all individual markers use the same traffic light 1–9. Red on the left, green on the right — higher is always better: 1–3 red, 4–6 amber, 7–9 green.

scaleZones.label: 1–3 · Red
scaleZones.text: Outside the optimal range. This is where the greatest leverage lies.

scaleZones.label: 4–6 · Amber
scaleZones.text: Average range with room for improvement.

scaleZones.label: 7–9 · Green
scaleZones.text: Within the optimal range. Maintain existing routines.

blocks.title: Important
blocks.text: This report is not a substitute for a sports medicine examination or performance diagnostics.
items: The four genetic variants are innate and are determined only once. Information and written consent are required before the genetic analysis (German Genetic Diagnostics Act, GenDG). Predictive genetic testing may only be conducted under the responsibility of appropriately qualified physicians; genetic counselling must be offered before and after the test (Sections 7 and 10 GenDG).
Only the eight microRNA values can change — they alone are suitable for monitoring progress.

blocks.caption: Results at a glance
blocks.title: Your seven assessments.
blocks.lead: Each assessment is derived from several microRNAs together. Sorted by value — the areas requiring the most action appear at the bottom.

blocks.title: What this means
blocks.text: Three values in the red range — load/stress level (2), nutritional status (3) and inflammation (3). Two of them — load and inflammation — depend on miR-146a-5p (overload miRNA, 2/9), the weakest individual marker in the profile; in total it feeds into four of the seven assessments. Nutritional status, by contrast, depends on the second-weakest marker, miR-22-5p (3/9).
items: Three values in the mid-range — injury risk, cardiovascular fitness and muscle status each sit at 5/9 and can be influenced directly through training.
One value in the green range — hydration status (8) is stable and should stay that way.
The interval to the next follow-up measurement is determined by the facility looking after you; your two previous measurements were around three months apart.

blocks.caption: Basis of the assessments
blocks.title: The eight microRNAs.
blocks.lead: The individual values from which the seven assessments are calculated. They too use the traffic light 1–9; higher is better.

Regulates muscle vitality and cellular protection.
Reflects the interplay of exercise, nutrition and lifestyle.

blocks.title: The key marker
blocks.text: At 2/9, miR-146a-5p is the weakest individual value and feeds into four of the seven assessments: load/stress level, inflammation, injury risk and cardiovascular fitness. A single marker therefore shapes a large part of the overall picture.
items: The two muscle markers miR-378a-3p and miR-101-3p are both in the green range at 7/9. The musculature itself is not the problem — recovery is.

items.name: Load / stress level
items.intro: From miR-146a-5p (2/9) and miR-20a-5p (4/9). Stress disturbs resting homeostasis and increases energy turnover — what matters is whether recovery offsets the load.
items.text: Your value is outside the optimal range — the weakest of the seven assessments. Reduce everyday stressors, avoid time pressure, periodise your training (1–2 training-free days per week, a recovery week every 2–4 weeks) and use relaxation techniques such as autogenic training or biofeedback.

items.name: Nutritional status
items.intro: From miR-30e-3p (4/9), miR-22-5p (3/9) and miR-19b-3p (4/9). Indicates vitamin and micronutrient requirements, including B vitamins, iron and magnesium.
items.text: Your value is outside the optimal range. Pay particular attention to fruit, vegetables and wholegrain products — rich in B vitamins, magnesium, iron and zinc. Magnesium from nuts and sunflower seeds, zinc from dairy products, cheese and pulses.

items.name: Inflammation
items.intro: From five microRNAs: miR-505-3p, miR-30e-3p, miR-22-5p, miR-20a-5p and miR-146a-5p. These markers map inflammatory regulation under training load; at the same time, physical exertion releases stress hormones.
items.text: Your value is outside the optimal range. Pay attention to recovery and sufficient sleep, to vitamin C and zinc from fruit, vegetables, broccoli and citrus fruits, and to relaxation, moderate exercise and a fibre-rich diet for the gut flora.

blocks.title: The common denominator
blocks.text: All three assessments include miR-146a-5p or miR-22-5p — the two weakest individual markers. Managing training load and recovery therefore acts on all three values at once, not just on one.

items.name: Injury risk & recovery
items.intro: From five microRNAs: miR-30e-3p, miR-22-5p, miR-146a-5p, miR-20a-5p and miR-505-3p. Insufficient recovery increases the risk of injury.
items.text: Your value is in the average range. Ensure sufficient recovery phases between training sessions and pay attention to warming up, stretching and cooling down. Your genetic assessment of muscle damage risk in the chapter “Three further genetic assessments” complements this value.

items.name: Cardiovascular fitness
items.intro: From miR-20a-5p (4/9), miR-146a-5p (2/9) and miR-505-3p (5/9). Describes how efficiently the heart pumps blood and oxygen around the body.
items.text: Your value is in the average range. Include endurance training at least twice a week — running, brisk walking, cycling, swimming or aqua aerobics, depending on your level of fitness.

items.name: Muscle status
items.intro: From miR-101-3p (7/9), miR-378a-3p (7/9), miR-19b-3p (4/9) and miR-30e-3p (4/9). Strength, explosive power and endurance depend on the muscle's state of fatigue and recovery.
items.text: Your value is in the average range. Include strength training at least twice a week as a full-body workout with weights or body weight, each time with a warm-up, cool-down and stretching phase.

items.name: Hydration status
items.intro: From miR-101-3p (7/9) and miR-378a-3p (7/9). Fluid losses through sweat and respiration impair bodily functions and performance.
items.text: Your value is within the optimal range. Continue to ensure at least two litres of fluid a day, including during training sessions.

blocks.caption: Genetics · innate, determined once
blocks.title: Your sport markers.
blocks.lead: Four genetic variants complementing the changeable microRNA values. They describe predispositions — not an evaluation and not a performance forecast — and are determined only once. Sport type · ACE and ACTN3: the combination of both variants determines the predisposition between endurance and strength.
rows: Influences the bradykinin–aldosterone system and thus oxygen utilisation.
Determines muscle fibre composition; the mixed form combines fast and slow fibres.
blocks.note: Your sport type on the scale endurance type — mixed type — strength type: predominantly strength type. You are predominantly the strength-sport type. Suitable activities are strength sports such as weightlifting, powerlifting or bodybuilding.

blocks.caption: Genetics · innate, determined once
blocks.title: Three further genetic assessments.
rows: Effect of exercise on body weight
Very good. You can lose weight very effectively through exercise — physical activity is a particularly effective lever for you.
No heightened motivation. Fixed appointments, training partners or class formats help more than good intentions.
Slightly elevated. Pay particular attention to warming up and to cooling down or stretching afterwards.
blocks.note: The scales of these four assessments indicate a position between two poles, not a traffic light: a sport type is neither good nor bad. Genetic variants are determined only once and remain unchanged for life.

blocks.caption: Where you stand
blocks.title: Nutrition and lifestyle habits.
blocks.lead: The radar shows how close your current habits are to the scientific reference values. The further out a factor lies, the more favourable — 10 is optimal.

scores.label: Stress
scores.text: The weakest factor in your self-report. It coincides with your weakest laboratory value (load/stress level 2/9) — both point in the same direction.

scores.label: Snacks & meat
scores.text: Both mid-range — the two dietary factors with the most room for improvement, in line with the nutritional status of 3/9.

scores.label: Tobacco · Fruit/vegetables · Fluids
scores.text: Clearly above average. The fluid value is consistent with your good hydration status (8/9).

blocks.note: An assessment of where you stand based on your self-report, not an individual diagnosis. In the case of illness or during special life stages, please have any major dietary changes supervised by a doctor.

blocks.caption: Trend
blocks.title: Two measurements compared.
blocks.lead: A comparison of your two measurements to date. Only measured values are shown — not a forecast.
blocks.note: The interval between the two measurements was around three months. Whether this interval is also appropriate for the next follow-up is determined by the facility looking after you.

blocks.title: What the trend shows
blocks.text: One improvement: nutritional status from 2 to 3 — the direction is right, but the value is still outside the optimal range.
items: Two deteriorations: load/stress level (3 → 2) and inflammation (4 → 3). Both include miR-146a-5p. Between the two measurements it was therefore the load side that worsened, not the performance side.
Four unchanged values: hydration, injury risk, cardiovascular fitness and muscle status have remained stable.

blocks.caption: Summary
blocks.title: Your focus: recovery.
blocks.lead: The profile is unusually clear-cut. The muscle markers are in the green range, the load and inflammation markers in the red — and both deteriorations since the first measurement are on the same side.

focuses.title: Manage your load before you train more
focuses.text: The weakest individual marker, miR-146a-5p (2/9), feeds into four of the seven assessments. Exactly two of them — load/stress level and inflammation — have deteriorated since November. As long as this value stays low, additional training works against you rather than for you. Specifically: one to two training-free days per week, a recovery week every two to four weeks, relaxation techniques in everyday life. In addition, kaempferol and vitamin D3 from the intervention list.

focuses.title: Micronutrients from food, not from supplements
focuses.text: Nutritional status (3/9) has improved from 2 to 3 — the direction is right. From the lifestyle radar, snacks and meat (5 out of 10 each) are the two levers with the most room for improvement. Focus on fruit, vegetables and wholegrains for B vitamins, magnesium, iron and zinc.

blocks.keepText: Hydration status (8/9) has been stable since the first measurement and matches your radar value for fluids (8/10). The two muscle markers are also in the green range at 7/9 each — the musculature is not the problem. Genetically, your FTO gene suggests that physical activity has a particularly strong effect on your body weight.
controlItems: The interval to the next follow-up measurement is determined by the facility looking after you. Your two previous measurements were around three months apart.
The four genetic variants remain unchanged and are not repeated.
For comparability, sample collection, time of day and the interval since the last training session should remain similar.

blocks.title: Questions about your report?
blocks.text: Discuss the results with the facility that carried out the sample collection. That is where the training and health context needed to interpret them is held.

legal.title: Sample report
legal.text: All values, genotypes and personal details in this document are fictitious and serve solely to illustrate the report format. This is not a real report.

legal.title: Interpretation
legal.text: This report is not a diagnosis and is not a substitute for medical advice, a sports medicine examination or performance diagnostics. The microRNA values describe a snapshot in time; the genetic variants describe predispositions, not diseases and not a performance forecast.

legal.title: Status of the analyses
legal.text: The analyses are laboratory services provided by our cooperation partner and are not CE-marked in vitro diagnostic devices. They serve consultation and monitoring and do not replace clinical diagnostics. The analyses are supplied to professional users only.

legal.title: Legal framework
legal.text: Genetic testing is subject to the German Genetic Diagnostics Act (GenDG); information and written consent are required before sample collection. Predictive genetic testing may only be conducted under the responsibility of appropriately qualified physicians; genetic counselling must be offered before and after the test (Sections 7 and 10 GenDG). The laboratory analysis is carried out by our cooperation partner. Polaris Diagnostics Europe GmbH is responsible for distribution and support. Please review food supplements individually and in consultation with a qualified professional.
